key_insight: A neural-network navigation policy optimized by a genetic algorithm can learn near-optimal minimum-time steering in 2D flows, matching analytical solutions and handling turbulent cases.
engineering_relevance: This offers a compact, parallelizable route-planning method for autonomous vehicles moving through complex fluids, with less manual reward design than reinforcement learning.
method: Encode the steering policy as a neural network mapping local state to control direction.
Use a genetic algorithm with selection and parameter mutation to evolve candidate policies; no crossover.
Benchmark against analytical/optimal-control solutions, Q-learning, and actor-critic methods in several 2D flow cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery of analytical and numerical optima in benchmark problems, better performance than Q-learning and one-step actor-critic, and robustness to start-point variation and unresolved turbulence when fluctuation velocity is small.
watch_item: Robustness is conditional: unresolved turbulent fluctuations must remain weak relative to the vessel’s slip velocity, so performance may degrade in stronger subgrid variability.
paper_title: Learning minimum-time navigation policies in two-dimensional flows with a genetic algorithm
